author: M. Okafor
body: Vetter have cancelled our 12 Oct slot. I pushed back on the phone — they have a genuine line deviation and cannot hold it. Nothing earlier across Ravensburg, Halle or Hameln. Escalating because this is the validation lot, not a routine batch.

author: Sourcing agent
body: Checked the master agreement: the booking was a non-committed capacity reservation, clause 7.3 permits reallocation on 30 days notice. No contractual claim and no penalty available. Scanned the ASL for alternative fill-finish capacity — Siegfried Hameln is approved, audit current to Mar 2028, already qualified for Berobenatide T2D and Sigvotatug, and has capacity from 29 Sep.
sourcesRead: master agreement clause 7.3, Approved Supplier List, audit validity

author: A. Kowalski
body: If we move site, it is a bracketed revalidation, not a full one, because the modality is unchanged. Realistically 21 days of protocol plus execution. I would want the protocol drafted against the Berobenatide T2D precedent so we are not writing it from scratch. Flagging that media-fill qualification on a new fill line has overrun 5–8 days on two of our last seven transfers.

author: S. Lindqvist
body: The bigger risk is not the 47 days, it is the CHMP review slot. We hold a Q4 window. If the dossier is not complete by mid-November we lose it and the next confirmed slot is February — that is another 31 days on top. Please treat the CHMP date as the real deadline.

author: Commercial agent
body: Iberia field-force certification at 91% against a 95% target. 14 reps pending a lab session. Rebooked all 14 into the 22 Sep cohort, which puts the region at 97% well before first ship.

author: T. Bergmann
body: Good. Keep the 22 Sep cohort protected — I do not want those slots reallocated.

author: D. Moreau
body: We missed the AMA panel cycle. Next submission window is February, decision September 2027 — six months after first ship. There is no route that recovers this.

author: H. Fossi
body: Escalating to the Launch Board. Launching in the US without a code, or holding the US back, is a commercial policy call — it is not mine and it is not the agent's.

author: Market Access agent
body: Both scenarios prepared for the Board pack. Launch without a code: miscellaneous J-code billing, 40% of target accounts likely to defer. Hold the US: €7.8M deferred to FY28, EU launch unaffected.

author: Supply Chain agent
body: 340 of 520 launch stock units are still awaiting their final QC release check. The 3PL is running a 6-day turnaround against a 4-day plan. At the current rate launch supply coverage is short by 11 days.

author: R. Devi
body: Pricing a second lane at Neuss. The alternative is shipping first cases with a reduced set count, which the MSLs will push back on. I will have a number by the 12th.

author: Quality agent
body: Sequence D of the cold-chain transit protocol battery produced visible deformation of the secondary carton on 3 of 12 units. Container closure integrity integrity held on all twelve. The protocol cannot be signed as-is.

author: K. Tanaka
body: Agreed, and I would not want to go to the CHMP rapporteur with a concession request on packaging. Redesigning the insert — it is a tooling change on the thermoform, not a formulation change. Re-test booked for the 14th.

author: Regulatory agent
body: Second query cycle opened on the clinical section. Response pack assembled from the CSR and the equivalence rationale — 14 pages, every query answered with a traced source. The 21-day clock-stop started 07 Sep. I cannot submit without a qualified signatory.

author: H. Fossi
body: Escalating. The pack has been complete since the 7th and every day of delay is a day of G4. Sofia, please review and sign.

author: H. Fossi
body: No response to the reminder. Raising to the Regulatory Director — this is now the single largest controllable risk on the programme.

author: K. Tanaka
body: Twelve of fourteen CMC deliverables are signed. The two outstanding are the human factors report and the transit summary, both of which the agent has drafted from the test data. I have reviewed both and I am content technically.

author: Quality agent
body: Both drafts traced to the design input matrix, no acceptance criteria waived. human factors summative passed with zero use errors in the critical tasks. cold-chain transit protocol Sequences A to D passed with the container closure integrity intact. Ready for signature.

author: Sourcing agent
body: Aptar downgraded to High financial risk — 34-day payables extension, second consecutive quarter. They are single source on the lyophilisation stopper across Berobenatide OB, Berobenatide T2D and two other Vaccines presentations.

author: M. Okafor
body: The second source is qualified and has capacity. The problem is timing: the BOM freezes at G2 on 30 Sep, so activating now is a document change. After the freeze it is a design change, and that is 11 weeks of change control across four launches.

author: T. Bergmann
body: Supporting activation. The premium is small against €6.2M of exposure, and we carry the same supplier on two other programmes.

author: Line Monitor agent
body: Berobenatide OB runs commercial output on lines 3 and 5. SPC rule 2 broken on line 3 — pulled and re-measured the commercial batches in the window and confirmed 3 out of spec on the dimensional check. For context, PPQ produces 3 batches as the norm (a validation run was 12 at one site), so 3 affected commercial batches is a full run's worth of supply. Line 5 is unaffected. Raised without anyone asking it to look.
sourcesRead: Line 3 MES, SPC control chart, commercial batch dimensional records

author: A. Kowalski
body: Line 5 is holding commercial supply for now, so this is not a stoppage question — it is a volume question. There is already a CAPA open on line 3 for the dimensional drift, and it is overdue: the DMAIC behind it is still in progress. Measure and Analyse are done and the drift points at tool wear, but Improve and Control are not signed, so I cannot re-qualify line 3 for commercial output yet. Until that closes we are producing fewer commercial batches than the launch plan assumed.

author: Planning agent
body: Modelled the shortfall against the launch plan. Losing line 3's 3 commercial batches leaves the launch quantity short, so either the volume is redistributed across markets (protect the lead markets, defer the lower-priority ones) or commercial output moves to another qualified site on the same modality. Checked the alternate-site option: a same-modality transfer avoids a requalification, but it is contingent on two confirmations — regulatory/engineering clearance for the site, and that the site actually has open capacity in the window. Both hold G3; the difference is where the reduced volume lands.
sourcesRead: Launch plan, commercial allocation model, qualified-site register, site capacity calendar

author: L. Haugen
body: So the real choice is between three moves. Re-prioritise markets and redistribute the reduced commercial volume — cleanest, and it keeps the lead-market quantities whole. Push the DMAICs to close the line-3 CAPA fast so we re-operate line 3 and recover the batches. Or move commercial output to another site on the same modality, once the agents confirm it is OK on regulatory/engineering and that the capacity is actually there. All three hold G3. This is above my line because prioritising markets is a commercial and planning trade-off, not a manufacturing one.

author: L. Haugen
body: Tooling and line time are booked from 02 Nov. If we do not release the build in the next week the slot goes to the Irvine transfer and we lose eight weeks. I cannot authorise this volume myself — the exposure is over the delegated limit.

author: Finance agent
body: Modelled three volumes against P50 demand. 4,200 units: €2.8M exposure, full launch cover. 2,600: €1.7M, covers the first 9 weeks in DE and FR and holds the G5 date. 1,400: €0.9M, stocks out in week 5. Recommending 2,600.
